hook.convey: closed shape → walk its edge from one corner back to the same corner → how far = perimeter

use.hi: Cricket ground ki boundary rope ke saath ek poora chakkar lagao, wahi corner jahan se shuru kiya tha
use.en: Walk once along the boundary rope of a cricket ground, back to the corner you started from

use.hi: Sabzi ke bagiche ki baad ke saath ek poora chakkar, jahan se shuru kiya wahin tak
use.en: Walk once along the fence of a vegetable garden, back to where you started

explain.convey: perimeter (parimap) = total length of the boundary → start at a corner, every side once, back to the start; triangle 4, 5, 6 cm → 15 cm

point.hi: triangle ki teeno bhujayein: 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm
point.en: the triangle's three sides: 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm

prompt.hi: Agar triangle ki bhujayein 3 cm, 4 cm aur 5 cm hon, toh parimap kitna hoga?
prompt.en: If a triangle's sides are 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm, what is its perimeter?

explain.convey: perimeter = AROUND (a length, cm or m); area = INSIDE; 6 cm by 4 cm card → edge 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm, not 6 × 4

point.hi: rectangle ka kinara: upar 6 cm, daayein 4 cm, neeche 6 cm, baayein 4 cm
point.en: the rectangle's edge: top 6 cm, right 4 cm, bottom 6 cm, left 4 cm

prompt.hi: Ek card 5 cm lamba aur 2 cm chauda hai. Uske kinare ki lambai kitni hogi?
prompt.en: A card is 5 cm long and 2 cm wide. How long is its edge?

problem.hi: Ek paanch bhujaon wali kyaari ki bhujayein 4 m, 5 m, 3 m, 6 m aur 2 m hain. Uske chaaron taraf ek baar baad lagani hai, kitni baad lagegi?
problem.en: A five-sided flower bed has sides 4 m, 5 m, 3 m, 6 m and 2 m. How much fencing goes once around it?

givens.hi: bhujayein: 4 m, 5 m, 3 m, 6 m, 2 m
givens.en: sides: 4 m, 5 m, 3 m, 6 m, 2 m

find.hi: kyaari ka parimap, yaani ek chakkar ki baad
find.en: the flower bed's perimeter: fencing once around

why.hi: baad kinare ke saath chalti hai, har bhuja ek baar
why.en: the fence runs along the edge, each side once

prompt.hi: Ab aakhri bhuja tum jodo: 18 m mein 2 m jodne par kitna?
prompt.en: Now you add the last side: 18 m plus 2 m makes how much?

why.hi: paanchon bhujayein ek-ek baar judi, aur jawab ek lambai hai, isliye m mein
why.en: all five sides added once each, and the answer is a length, so in m

prompt.hi: Ek L shape ke kamre ki 6 bhujayein hain: 8 m, 3 m, 5 m, 4 m, 3 m aur 7 m. Kamre ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: An L-shaped room has 6 sides: 8 m, 3 m, 5 m, 4 m, 3 m and 7 m. What is the room's perimeter?

prompt.hi: Ek card ki bhujayein 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm aur 4 cm hain. Uske kinare par ek chakkar ke liye kitni lace chahiye?
prompt.en: A card has sides 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm and 4 cm. How much lace goes once around its edge?

ladder.why: first straight use: triangle, add all sides
perimeter vs area from the situation

remediation.move: ant walk with a running total after each side, until it is back at the start corner

say.hi: Ek cheenti corner se chalti hai aur har bhuja ke baad apna total badhati hai. Jab tak wapas shuruaat wale corner par na aaye, chakkar poora nahi hota
say.en: An ant starts at a corner and adds to its total after every side. The round is not done until it is back at the start corner

prompt.hi: Ek 6 bhujaon wale khet ki bhujayein 10 m, 4 m, 6 m, 5 m, 4 m aur 9 m hain. Uska parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: A 6-sided field has sides 10 m, 4 m, 6 m, 5 m, 4 m and 9 m. What is its perimeter?

remediation.move: string on the edge vs tiles inside: the edge is a length, the inside is a covering

say.hi: Parimap kinare par rakhi dori ki lambai hai. Andar ki jagah dhakna area hai, woh alag cheez hai
say.en: Perimeter is the length of a string laid on the edge. Covering the inside is area, a different thing

prompt.hi: Ek label 5 cm lamba aur 3 cm chauda hai. Uske kinare par ek chakkar ka ribbon kitna lamba hoga?
prompt.en: A label is 5 cm long and 3 cm wide. How long is a ribbon once around its edge?

bridgeToNext.hi: Har bhuja jodna hamesha kaam karta hai. Ab rectangle aur square mein bhujayein jodi mein aati hain, toh ek chhota tareeka milega
bridgeToNext.en: Adding every side always works. Rectangles and squares have sides in pairs, so there is a shorter way
